slides.title: Satisfaction Scores Diverge Sharply by Company Size
slides.insight: Enterprise customers are universally satisfied (100% rating 4–5), while SMBs cluster at neutral — signaling an unmet-needs gap that grows as company size shrinks.

slides.title: Respondent Mix by Region
slides.insight: Over half the sample is North American, so regional sub-groups (especially Asia-Pacific at n = 4) should be interpreted directionally rather than definitively.

slides.title: Feature Adoption Varies Dramatically by Company Size
slides.insight: Enterprise customers are heavy users of Integrations (100%) and AI Insights (100%), while SMBs rely almost entirely on Alerts and Exports — suggesting smaller firms haven't discovered the platform's advanced capabilities.

slides.title: 30-Day Purchase Rate by Region & Gender
slides.insight: North America drives purchasing at 75%, while Europe's 60% non-purchase rate suggests a conversion bottleneck — possibly pricing or localization friction.

slides.title: Rating Dimensions by Company Size: Enterprise Outperforms Across the Board
slides.insight: Enterprise users rate every dimension 4.5+ out of 5 while SMBs average below 3 — the experience gap is systemic, not limited to a single touchpoint.

slides.title: Recommendations
bullets: Prioritize the SMB onboarding experience: satisfaction and trust scores are critically low — consider guided setup flows or dedicated CSM touchpoints for smaller accounts.
Drive feature discovery for non-Enterprise tiers: Integrations and AI Insights have 0% adoption among SMBs despite being the features most correlated with high satisfaction.
Investigate the Europe conversion gap: a 60% non-purchase rate vs. 25% in North America points to possible pricing, localization, or go-to-market issues worth a dedicated follow-up study.

Expand the Mobile App experience: at 57% adoption vs. 90% for Website, there's significant room to shift engagement toward mobile — especially for the 35–54 cohort that already indexes high on app usage.
Caveat: all sub-groups carry low-base warnings (n < 30). Validate these directional findings with a larger-scale study before making major resource commitments.
